title: Representation of the derived product of a tower
statement:
Let $\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T)$ be the tower category of
[def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and let $M_\bullet\in
D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$. Choose a complex $C_\bullet$ of towers representing $M_\bullet$ and a K-injective resolution
[def-sp-kinjective-bridge] $C_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ in the abelian
category of towers. Write $M_n=\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet$. Then the derived product $R\!\prod_nM_n$ of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] is represented by
$\prod_n\operatorname{ev}_n(I_\bullet)$.

Here the product complex is formed in $\Mod(T_{\Proet},A_T)$, and is read in its derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; its degree-$q$ term is $\prod_{n\geq1}(\operatorname{ev}_nI_\bullet)^q$, with differential determined by its composites with the projections. The source is Stacks Tag 07KC (label lemma-products): exact countable products allow termwise products of any representatives. Tag 0BK6 is an alternative when the individual representatives are known to be K-injective; that additional assertion is not needed here.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\Mod(T_{\Proet},A_T)$, where $A_T$ is the coefficient sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Apply [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] with $Y=T$ and $\mathcal R=A_T$. Thus $\mathcal A$ has exact countable products. This uses the actual sheaf $A_T$, not its discrete quotient coefficient rings.

source.place: Propositions 3.1.9, 3.2.3(1), 4.2.8, as stated for module sheaves by lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact

proof.text: Use the chosen representative $C_\bullet$ and its given resolution map $C_\bullet\to I_\bullet$. By [def-sp-kinjective-bridge] this map is a quasi-isomorphism. Kernels, images, and cokernels of towers are computed levelwise by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], so $H^q(\operatorname{ev}_n C_\bullet)=\operatorname{ev}_n H^q(C_\bullet)$ and likewise for $I_\bullet$. The evaluation of the resolution therefore induces an isomorphism on every cohomology object. By the localization definition [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $Q(\operatorname{ev}_n I_\bullet)$ is a representative of $\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet$ for each $n$. Only the quasi-isomorphism part of the resolution hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 015F, label lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, proof; exact evaluation preserves cohomology by levelwise kernels and cokernels

proof.text: Form $P^q=\prod_{n\geq1}(\operatorname{ev}_n I_\bullet)^q$ in $\mathcal A$. Define $d_P^q$ by $\mathrm{pr}_n d_P^q=d_n^q\mathrm{pr}_n$; its square is zero since this holds after every projection. The projections form the termwise product cone. Apply [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core] to $\mathcal A$ and this countable family of complexes, using Step 1 for exact countable products. It states that the image under $Q$ of every termwise product cone is limiting. Hence $Q(P)$, with these projections, is the product of the objects $Q(\operatorname{ev}_n I_\bullet)$ in $D(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Tag 07KC, label lemma-products, statement (2) applied to evaluated tower representatives

proof.text: The derived product of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] is the product of $\operatorname{ev}_n M_\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal A)$. Let $\alpha_n:Q(\operatorname{ev}_nI_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet$ be the isomorphisms of Step 2. Give $Q(P)$ projections $\alpha_n\circ Q(\mathrm{pr}_n)$. For a family $g_n:L\to\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet$, the limiting cone of Step 3 has a unique lift of the family $\alpha_n^{-1}\circ g_n$. This is exactly the required unique lift to the new cone. The product universal property [def-weil-category-product] therefore identifies this cone with $R\!\prod_nM_n$, proving the claimed representation.

Made the complex representative explicit, replaced the etale-only K-injective definition by the general bridge, and corrected the ambient category of the product. No new nodes.
